Exasperate

/ig-ZAS-puh-rayt/ - the stress falls on ZAS · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Exasperate means to irritate; to wear out someone's patience.

The toddler's forty-minute bedtime negotiations could exasperate even the family's calmest babysitter.

Worked Example

Rehearsals began to exasperate the director for a new reason each night: the lead had taken to improving lines that were already perfect, differently every evening, and defending each version with a bow.

Exasperate names the far end of annoyance — the point where patience is not just tested but used up. A dripping tap annoys; a tap that drips only when the plumber has left exasperates. Its unit cousin vex stays milder and smaller.

How Exasperate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

frustrate

frustrate: to block someone's efforts until they fume

madden

madden: to push irritation toward fury

Antonyms

calm

calm: to settle someone's ruffled patience

gratify

gratify: to please and satisfy instead of grate

How Strong Is It? — annoy → exasperate → enrage

annoy vs. exasperate

annoy vs. exasperate: Annoy is milder than exasperate — an annoyance buzzes at your patience without draining it.

enrage vs. exasperate

enrage vs. exasperate: Enrage is stronger than exasperate: exasperation is patience worn through, while rage has left patience behind entirely.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ex-

Prefix — ex-: thoroughly (Latin)

Root — asper

Root — asper: rough (Latin asper)

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: verb-forming ending

Put it together

Put it together: Ex- (thoroughly) + asper (rough) + -ate = to roughen thoroughly. Latin exasperare meant to make a surface rough — and, soon enough, to rub a person's temper raw. Whatever exasperates you is sandpaper applied to your patience.

Use the root in a new word: asperity

Use the root in a new word: asperity: There was a new asperity in the coach's voice after the third fumble — a roughness that made the bench sit very straight.

Word Choice

neutral

Exasperate is annoyance at the end of its rope — use it when patience has been worn through by repetition or absurdity. For a passing irritation, its unit neighbor vex is lighter; when anger takes over, you have moved past exasperation into fury.
